active_probe_mechanism.conclusion: Copy, recall, counter, and recomputation effects are heterogeneous; the data do not support a monotonic chore-complexity claim.

supported.claim: Active recomputation usually reduced success, but not universally: 6/7 point estimates were negative, 3 paired 95% intervals excluded zero below, and one stratum was positive.
supported.qualification: Seven model-by-benchmark strata are descriptive replications, not independent samples for a pooled universal claim.

supported.claim: Signal quality is conditional: active recomputation has the highest AUPRC in 3/7 powered slices; another passive method or a context/clock baseline leads 4/7.
supported.qualification: Active signals are measured on carried trajectories and zero-carry signals on clean trajectories; this is an ecological comparison, not a same-trajectory counterfactual.

supported.claim: Provider-backed active and passive observation both consume calls, tokens, elapsed compute, and dollars; deterministic trace rules, clocks, and context-use add zero provider calls.
supported.qualification: Passive provider latency is off the target path and must not be described as agent delay.

supported.claim: Natural-policy deployment is method-by-operator specific. Descriptive leaders were No state action: Frozen quiz, Trace rules (0.750); Lossy compaction: Frozen recompute (0.800); Public-state reground: Active recompute (0.850); quote-only WATCH reminder: Trace rules (0.825).
supported.qualification: Use the exact paired intervals, action incidence, and interactions—not point-estimate ranks alone. Deployment covers Luna on 40 Evolving Intent tasks only.

supported.claim: The paired n=38 cumulative two-source-task omission audit assessment is `scientific_outcome_conclusion_changed`.
supported.qualification: Report every outcome/action/resource flag listed in the sensitivity receipt, including any changed conclusion.

supported.claim: Under the common aggressive checkpoint-1 schedule, the best point estimate depends on the state operator; no method is universally dominant.
supported.qualification: The yoked study reuses the same 40 source tasks and is neither natural timing nor an independent replication.

unsupported.claim: Active observation always harms task success.
unsupported.reason: One of seven powered active-recompute effects is positive; four intervals include zero.

unsupported.claim: Observer harm is consistent without exceptions across four or five powered models.
unsupported.reason: The result is a 6/7 trend with a positive Luna/Evolving exception, not a rule.

unsupported.claim: Active signals are universally less accurate than passive signals or trivial baselines.
unsupported.reason: Active recomputation leads AUPRC in some powered slices.

unsupported.claim: Passive signals universally outperform clock and context baselines.
unsupported.reason: Powered signal winners vary by model and benchmark.

unsupported.claim: Increasing active chore complexity monotonically improves detection or worsens observer harm.
unsupported.reason: The n=20 mechanism arms are heterogeneous and explicitly exploratory.

unsupported.claim: Evolving Intent supplies independently graded within-N-turn degradation labels.
unsupported.reason: It supplies verified final success; BFCL supplies turn-level action-failure evidence.

unsupported.claim: The deployed feedback is an LLM-generated GOOD/BAD decision critique.
unsupported.reason: It is a deterministic, bounded, quote-only WATCH reminder.

unsupported.claim: Primary online intervention counts are matched across methods.
unsupported.reason: The primary study uses unequal natural scalar firing rates with a one-action cap.

unsupported.claim: Deployment results generalize across models or to action traces.
unsupported.reason: Deployment covers one model and one reasoning benchmark; BFCL was not deployed.

unsupported.claim: The final deployment has a truly unmonitored arm or an oracle bound.
unsupported.reason: operator=none is monitored no-action; neither final manifest includes an oracle.

online_natural_policy.interpretation: These are deployed-policy comparisons under unequal natural scalar firing rates; they combine method identity with realized firing/action behavior.

yoked_checkpoint1_sensitivity.interpretation: Controlled sensitivity on the same 40 tasks with one active-anchored action at checkpoint 1; not natural timing and not an independent replication.

disclosures.online: Three passive trace-judge cells spanning two of 40 deployment source tasks required same-prefix semantic recovery after output-cap truncation. Cell 89df recovered checkpoint 6 with cap 640; cell 786 used cap 640 at checkpoints 5 and 6. Executor attribution for the 89df and 786 recovery suffixes is unknown. Raw production artifacts were retained; a hash-bound copy counted every physical attempt and normalized one ordinary HTTP 503 ledger status, and a paired n=38 sensitivity omitted both affected source tasks from all 28 treatments.
disclosures.two_pass: The two-pass passive pass had one documented trace-judge recovery. Trace judge was not among the four methods selected for the final active-anchored yoked schedule; the recovery remains part of the reproducibility record.

active_vs_frozen_recompute.semantics: Active elapsed time is on the target path; frozen elapsed time is off-path compute and is not target delay.

observer_overhead.conclusion: Zero-carry does not mean zero-cost: provider-backed passive monitors add calls, tokens, latency, and dollars, while deterministic rules, clock, and context-use add no provider calls.
